name: CorkHook beforeSwap missing pool-manager restriction
summary: The incident combined a rollover-pricing defect that let the attacker acquire an excessive CT position for dust with CorkHook.beforeSwap() lacking the authorization check that restricted calls to the official Uniswap v4 PoolManager. A direct call to the hook abused its callback and refund path to obtain matching DS, and the attacker redeemed the CT/DS pair against the protocol's wstETH reserves.
notes: The direct CorkHook runtime was CREATE2-deployed in this transaction and remained unchanged through the exploit.

Cork reports 3,761 wstETH extracted, and the selected transaction records exactly 3,760.885365943909071528 wstETH transferred from ModuleCore to the attack contract. Verichains values the incident at approximately $12 million; the USD amount is the reported rounded valuation of this onchain asset outflow.
The $12 million USD loss is a rounded reported valuation; the exact onchain outflow is 3,760.885365943909071528 wstETH.
The campaign combined the measured CorkHook authorization defect with a separate rollover-pricing defect; this target records the defect-executing Hook artifact.
